newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh PM Sheikh Hasina leaves for China.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh PM Sheikh Hasina leaves for China.

text.p: Bangladesh Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina left for China on Thursday on a five-day visit which officials expect will usher in closer economic and defence ties.
"China is a neighbouring country and we want to develop further our trade and economic ties with China," Hasina said before boarding the plane on her first official visit since taking office in June.
Foreign Minister Abdus Samad Azad, accompanying Hasina, said she would discuss with Premier Li Peng issues ranging from boosting trade and investment to expanding defence cooperation.
Hasina will also meet Chinese President Jiang Zemin and Defence Minister General Chi Haotian. China is Bangladesh's main supplier of military hardware, a defence source in Dhaka said.
Trade between the two countries is growing but is in favour of Beijing.

Officials said Chinese exports to Bangladesh surged to $500 million in fiscal 1995-96 (July-June) from $120 million in 1991-92. China's imports from Bangladesh were a paltry $26 million in 1995-96, down $20 million from the previous year.
Last year, Dhaka persuaded Beijing to accept commodities as repayment for a $100 million Chinese loan instead of cash.
Dhaka and Beijing were expected to sign at least four agreements during Hasina's visit on avoidance of double taxation, investment and a soft loan from China, officials said.
"An understanding on setting up a coal-fired power plant in northern Bangladesh with Chinese assistance is also likely," one official said.
Hasina would visit Hong Kong on her way home to address a select gathering of leading corporate investors, foreign ministry officials said.
